responses.diagnosis: The lint step rejects an unused binding x. The test never ran. Do not invent a different root cause without source usage evidence.

blockers.verification: Inspect whether x is needed for behavior; if not, remove it; otherwise implement its actual use. Lint pass alone cannot prove intended functionality.

responses.closure: After an authorized fix, run lint and dependent tests on the exact new FIX_HEAD; unchanged historical attempt remains failed.

responses.diagnosis: The unresolved crate::cache import is only observed on logged commit c; the requested b commit has no supported failure status.

blockers.cause: Missing module versus feature-gated module at c
blockers.verification: Check module existence and feature selection on c; retrieve b build/attempt evidence independently before requested-head conclusion.

responses.closure: A fresh run on the specifically requested b or authorized later FIX_HEAD is required for closure.

responses.diagnosis: The first clock assertion failed, but a later retry passed; no actual source repair was demonstrated.

blockers.verification: Run targeted test with injected deterministic clock and recorded runner scheduling; classify whether failure vanishes under clock control or follows runner load despite controlled clock.

responses.closure: Repeated representative exact-head passes with a supported cause are necessary; the one green retry is not a defect fix.

responses.diagnosis: Linux eslint parsing and Windows path-separator assertion are two coexisting failures. They are not A/B alternatives.

blockers.verification: Parse affected source under the configured ESLint dialect and inspect the exact line; discriminate parser setting from invalid syntax.
Compare platform path API contract to observed and expected separators in the Windows fixture.

responses.closure: Both independent checks and their required dependents must pass on the same verified post-fix head.

evidence: No OOM-killer event or runner termination reason attached
responses.diagnosis: Exit 137 is consistent with SIGKILL, not proof of out-of-memory. There is no same-attempt OOM evidence.

blockers.verification: Correlate cgroup OOM-kill counters and memory peak with runner cancellation/stop records; each produces different evidence.

responses.closure: Require a cause-specific change plus a fresh exact-head integration run, never infer recovery from an absent error.

evidence: No runner clock or certificate chain included
responses.diagnosis: Certificate verification claims expiry; evidence cannot distinguish expired leaf/intermediate chain from runner clock skew.

blockers.cause: Leaf expiry, intermediate expiry or untrusted runner time
blockers.verification: Compare presented leaf and intermediates against independently trusted UTC and runner clock. Valid chain with skewed clock implicates time; expired leaf or intermediate at trusted time implicates certificate chain.

responses.closure: Observe a normal TLS-validated installation and dependent tests on the verified repaired head, no bypass.

responses.diagnosis: Artifact upload got HTTP 403 insufficient scope. A multi-line synthetic authorization header was redacted; no actual exposure is proved.

blockers.cause: Insufficient permission scope versus wrong token audience
blockers.verification: Authorized owner inspects protected scope/audience metadata, with separate credential exposure assessment; never reconstruct or disclose the token.

responses.closure: On authorized head, upload and dependent publish must both execute; disclosure review separate.

evidence: Output truncated; no individual step, command, or error

responses.closure: Request exact revision/attempt step log and its first failing command before proposing any cause or code fix.
